person_note: The ordinary character chapters use sustained third-person limited narration, as demonstrated by the Goodreads passages about Harper, Reed, and Tabitha and corroborated by commercial structural guides. Separate Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard chapters constitute collective first-person narration: the islands or their communities speak as 'we/us,' first in the opening and again in an interior Nantucket section. Because these are autonomous recurring base sections rather than isolated speech or maxims, the novel alternates first- and third-person narration. Confidence is medium because the recurring structure is supported by Goodreads plus several agreeing commercial guides, but no accessible authorized or scholarly whole-book source was found.
